blocker_resolution.round_1_blocker: Frontier-trend inference ignored selection on records (monotone-by-construction subset, vacuous P-values, biased sigma/HDIs).
blocker_resolution.verdict: RESOLVED, verified in code and outputs, not just prose.
evidence: run.py step 5 pops P(beta>0) from frontier summaries; every frontier row in frontier_summary.csv / cross_task.csv / headline.json carries an explicit selection_note; the round-1 P-values (>0.999, 0.976, 0.9995) and the 'suggestive deceleration' P(beta2<0)=0.875 are explicitly retracted in FINDINGS findings 6-7.

selection.py implements three selection-aware replacements: (i) exact record-count test (records among J exchangeable values, p_i=1/i Poisson-binomial) - reviewer verified the pmf by brute-force permutation enumeration (j=6, max abs diff 6e-17) and reproduced the quoted p-values exactly (J=12: P(K>=6)=0.03417, P(K>=7)=0.00632; J=8: P(K>=6)=0.00871); (ii) flat-null record-slope calibration from a no-slope refit posterior with the real design (dates, capped Ns, binomial noise) - honestly concludes the record slope carries ~no trend information (p=0.51/0.52); (iii) linear-PPC quadratic check that correctly nulls out the mechanical deceleration of record paths (p=0.43/0.72 - saturation claim withdrawn).

The exact exchangeable p-value is cross-validated by the design-matched flat-null simulation (0.0342 exact vs 0.034 sim; 0.0087 vs 0.0075), which covers the heterogeneous-N objection to the exchangeability null.

Release-date ties handled correctly: observed statistics enumerated over all tie-consistent orderings, p-values quoted at the conservative ordering, simulations randomise tie order per rep. Reviewer independently recomputed the record sets and counts (cybench 6-7 of 12, intercode 6 of 8) and the observed record-path OLS slope/quad (3.195/-0.955; 1.013/1.199) - all match frontier_null.csv.
growth_curves.png labels the dashed line 'record path (descriptive; rises by construction)'.

suggestions: FINDINGS.md is 156 lines vs the ~150-line contract; trim a few lines if regenerating.

Finding 3 (P(beta_cybench > beta_intercode)=0.98) treats the two task posteriors as independent, but all 8 intercode models also appear in the cybench fit; task-correlated model idiosyncrasies would correlate the posterior errors (positive correlation would make 0.98 conservative, but the assumption deserves one caveat line).

Finding 2's 'positive' verdict for intercode rests materially on the record-count test (base-prior HDI lower bound is +0.004 and the wide-prior HDI marginally includes 0); consider making that reliance explicit in the finding's wording, e.g. 'positive (marginal on the mean trend; corroborated by the selection-free record test, P=0.009)'.
